title: Button's Lost Sparkly Shell
markdown:
The sun’s golden fingers stretched over the tallest greenest trees. Beams, warm and soft as butter melting, trickled through Mimi the monkey’s window. Mimi did not just wake up. She sprang with a lively bounce.

“Hooray.” Her voice was a bubbly delight. Today felt truly fantastic, bursting with possibilities.

Then a tiny soft sigh floated from Button the bear cub’s cozy corner. His fuzzy brown ears drooped like sleepy sunflowers.

Mimi, always quick and curious, bounded over, long tail giving a little twitch. “What’s the matter, Button?”

Button blinked his big gentle brown eyes. A little cloud seemed to hover there. “My shell,” he mumbled. “My very favorite sparkly shell. It’s gone.”

Mimi’s tail twitched more energetically. Button loved his sparkly shell. It winked and shimmered with all the colours of a tiny rainbow.

“Oh no. Don’t be sad, Button. We can’t have you feeling glum on such a bright day. We’ll find it. I promise.” She took his soft paw. “Let’s go on a grand shell-finding adventure.”

They dashed out, a whirlwind of fur and giggles. Cool morning air, fresh and dewy, tickled their noses. The path wiggled and bounced like a playful snake toward the big sparkling blue sea.

Then, as they rounded a cluster of bright green bushes, they saw it. A big old wicker basket had tipped over near the rockpools. Shells everywhere, twinkling as if a treasure chest had burst open on the sand. Pretty pink ones. Pearly white ones. Swirly ones like tiny ice cream cones. Bumpy ones that felt like little buttons.

“Wow,” Button breathed, sadness vanishing. Wide-eyed wonder.

“Look at them all.” Mimi giggled and did a little happy spin. “They’re like little jewels from the sea.” Then a tiny shadow crossed her face. She remembered. “But where’s your special sparkly one, Button?”

They began to pick up shell after shell. Mimi found the little flat ones, like tiny perfect pancakes, and placed them near a flat grey rock. Button discovered the bumpy ones, wonderfully tickly against his paws, and tucked them near a craggy brown stone with interesting little holes. Long thin shells made a gentle whistling when the sea breeze blew past. Mimi found a sunny spot and let the wind play a little tune. Each shell seemed to have its own special place.

“Hmm.” Mimi tapped a tiny smooth shell and tilted her head. “This little one looks like it belongs in that rockpool over there. See? The one with the tiny bright blue pebbles shimmering at the bottom.”

Button nodded. “And this swirly one looks like a tiny empty castle. It looks so happy next to that big green waving seaweed.”

They became a super shell-sorting team, paws busy, hearts light. Flat shells into flat rockpools. Round shells into little round nooks. They giggled and chattered, sharing discoveries. Button was having a wonderful time helping all the shells find their homes. Still he kept looking around, soft brown eyes searching for that one special twinkle. A tiny soft sigh, almost too quiet to hear.

“It’s a little bit tricky, Mimi,” he said quietly. A hint of the earlier sadness. “There are so many different rockpools. What if we just can’t find mine?”

Mimi paused. She saw her friend looking a little glum. She looked at the pools. Some big and splashy, some small and hidden. Some filled with colourful shiny pebbles, some draped with waving green seaweed. Then her bright eyes spotted it. A little further down the beach, tucked between two big grey rocks, a very special rockpool. Filled with the smoothest tiniest pebbles, gleaming like little silver beads. The most perfect home for a very sparkly shell.

“Button.” She whispered, sudden excitement. She pointed. “Look. Over there.”

With a burst of speed she scrambled to the little pool and peeked over the edge. Her heart thumped a happy little rhythm. There, nestled among the smooth grey pebbles, winking and sparkling in the bright warm sun, was Button’s shell. All the colours of the rainbow, more beautiful than ever.

“I found it. I found it.” Carefully she scooped it up.

She raced back, holding it out like a magnificent prize. Button’s face lit brighter than the morning sun. He took his shell and held it tight against his furry chest.

“Oh, Mimi. Thank you.” He gave her a big happy bear hug that squeezed all the happiness into the air between them.

They looked at the last few shells, still waiting patiently.

“We did it,” Mimi cheered. “We helped all the shells find their homes.”

Button beamed, the sparkly shell twinkling like a happy star in his paw. They did not say the adventure was just beginning. They only set the last whistling shell where the breeze could find it, then raced off together, feet bouncing on the sand, Button’s shell winking in his fist like a piece of the sea that had agreed to come home.
